{{short description|Result in field theory about zeros of formal power series}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Strassmann's theorem''' is a result in [[field theory (mathematics)|field theory]]. It states that, for suitable fields, suitable formal [[power series]] with coefficients in the [[valuation ring]] of the field have only finitely many zeroes.

==History==
It was introduced by [[Reinhold Strassmann|Reinhold Strassman]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Straßmann |first=Reinhold |date=1928 |title=Über den Wertevorrat von Potenzreihen im Gebiet der -adischen Zahlen. |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/crll.1928.159.13/html |journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]] |language=en |volume=1928 |issue=159 |pages=13–28 |doi=10.1515/crll.1928.159.13 |issn=1435-5345|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Statement of the theorem==
Let <math>K</math> be a field with a [[Absolute value (algebra)|non-Archimedean absolute value]] <math>|\cdot|</math> and let <math>R</math> be the [[valuation ring]] of <math>K</math>. Let <math>f(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + a_2 x^2 + \dots</math> be a formal power series which is not identically zero, with coefficients <math>a_n \in R</math> converging to zero with respect to <math>|\cdot|</math>. Then <math>f(x)</math> has only finitely many zeroes in <math>R</math>. More precisely, the number of zeros is at most <math>N</math>, where <math>N</math> is the largest index with <math>|a_N| = \max_{n \geq 0} |a_n|</math>.

== Applications ==
A corollary of the theorem is that there is no analogue of [[Euler's identity]], <math>e^{2 \pi i} = 1</math> in <math>\mathbb{C}_p</math>, the field of [[P-adic number|p-adic]] complex numbers.

Strassman's theorem may also be used to prove the [[Skolem–Mahler–Lech theorem|Skolem-Mahler-Lech theorem]], which states that the set of indices at which a [[Constant-recursive sequence|linear recurrence sequence]] is equal to zero is composed of a union of finitely many arithmetic progressions and a finite set. 

== Related results ==
The [[Weierstrass preparation theorem#Formal power series in complete local rings|Weierstrass preparation theorem]] over complete local rings generalises Strassman's theorem. While Strassman's theorem states that <math>f(x)</math> has at most <math>N</math> zeros in <math>R</math>, a corollary of the Weierstrass preparation theorem is that <math>f(x)</math> has '''exactly''' <math>N</math> zeros in the valuation ring of the [[algebraic closure]] of <math>K</math>.
